```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 1](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop1.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the `command_line` folder:

```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
pwd
```

Replace the text below each heading with your own notes. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk like the one above.

## Basic unix commands

Notes on `pwd`, `ls`, `cd` and how unit commands are put together.

ls - function is used to list the names of all objects, variables, data frames, and functions currently stored in your active R environment

pwd - print working directory

cd - change directory

## Viewing and searching files

Notes on `cat`, `head`, `grep` and `man`.

cat - stands for "concatenate and print"

head - used to preview the first few rows or elements of a data object

grep - is a built-in function used to search for specific text patterns (or regular expressions) inside a collection of text

man - a Linux Manual Page Reader used in the Terminal tab inside RStudio to view documentation for operating system commands

## Sequence file formats

Notes on the fasta and fastq formats.

fasta - a function used to import, export, or analyze biological sequence data (such as DNA, RNA, or protein sequences stored in a .fasta file format) using R code

fastq - a function used to read, write, or analyze FASTQ files—which are text files storing biological sequences (like DNA or RNA) and their corresponding quality scores—using specialized R packages like ShortRead, dada2, or microseq
